summary: Franklin County, ME: 36-ft steel tower erected 1914, destroyed by lightning 1926 and rebuilt, turned into a radio tower in the early 1970s, removed in the 1990s; AT crosses the summit.

facts.design: 36-foot steel tower with a house or cab on top
facts.status_note: Converted to a radio tower in the early 1970s and removed in the 1990s; lookout footings remain on the summit

access.note: The Appalachian Trail crosses the summit

visit.trail_note: Reached on the Appalachian Trail; lookout footings are on the summit

events.note: Telephone line and equipment ordered for the lookout station (1914 forest commissioner report, as transcribed by Forest Lookouts)
Thirty-six-foot steel tower erected with a house or cab on top, and a log camp for the watchman. The Sun Journal list gives 1913 instead.
Kenneth Lee to be in charge of the station; he and his bride Ethel M. Wade to live in a log cabin on the summit
Demolished by a lightning bolt in summer 1926, just after the watchman climbed down
Replacement tower rising on the summit by September 1926
Warden James Parker manned the tower; building materials flown and trucked to the summit for a warden's camp close to the tower
Shortened and converted to a radio tower in the early 1970s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Sun Journal list gives 1913 for the tower. Forest Lookouts quotes the 1914 forest commissioner report and WillhiteWeb says the tower was erected in 1914. The story uses 1914 and says the sources differ by a year.

notes_for_editor: Build year disputed (1913 Sun Journal; 1914 forest report and WillhiteWeb). Summit elevation also disputed (4,456 ft in a 1917 newspaper quote, 4,116 ft in the 1954 article, 4,120 ft on WillhiteWeb); not used. Forest Fire Lookout Association Maine Chapter Facebook posts, seen only as search snippets and not readable through fetch_text, say a watchman's camp was built on the summit in 1954 and the tower closed in 1968; not used because the text could not be cached for quote checks, and 1968 conflicts with the early-1970s radio conversion. Worth a human look. The 36-foot figure supports the brief's height_m of 11.0.
